paper.title_en: ZTF J2229+1928: A 23 Minute Eclipsing Double White Dwarf Binary
paper.abstract_en: We report the discovery of ZTF J2229+1928, a detached and eclipsing DA double white dwarf binary in a 23-minute orbit. The system was identified in a GPU-accelerated search of ZTF photometry and confirmed through follow-up observations with the high speed imager proto-Lightspeed on the 6.5-meter Magellan Clay telescope. Combining the proto-Lightspeed eclipse model with mass-radius relations gives component radii and masses of $R_1 = 0.0146^{+0.0009}_{-0.0008} \, R_\odot$, $R_2 = 0.0186^{+0.0010}_{-0.0008} \, R_\odot$, and $M_1 = 0.49^{+0.08}_{-0.07} \, M_\odot$, $M_2 = 0.37^{+0.06}_{-0.05} \, M_\odot$. Fitting the Keck/LRIS spectra gives component temperatures of approximately $11,100$ K and $8,200$ K, and scaling this model to the broadband spectral energy distribution gives a distance of $\sim965$ pc. Its short orbital period places it firmly in the millihertz gravitational-wave regime, and we estimate an expected signal-to-noise ratio $\mathrm{SNR} \approx 5.3$ with the upcoming LISA mission over its nominal four-year duration. ZTF J2229+1928 thus adds to the small but growing sample of eclipsing ultracompact binaries that will serve as important sources for future space-based gravitational-wave observatories.
